rows.grounds: compound of kaniṣṭhā (little finger) and agra (tip), indicating the point of contact
optative indicating the prescribed condition or procedure
compound of gandha (fragrance) and dhāraṇa (retention/holding), locative of context

items.question: What corrective finger contact is prescribed during fragrance retention when the primary grip slips?
premises: The primary finger grip may slip during retention practice.
Fragrance retention requires a specified corrective contact.
Touching the little-finger tip constitutes that corrective contact.
items.inference: Therefore, during fragrance retention, one should touch the little-finger tip.
items.plain_english: In the retention of fragrance, one should touch the tip of the little finger.
